title: M101 Unit 7 · Linear approximation and numerical derivatives
rows: $L(a+h)=f(a)+f\prime(a)h$. Require a finite derivative at $a$; $h$ is a signed input change. Estimated change: $f\prime(a)h$.
$r(h)=f(a+h)-L(a+h)$ satisfies $r(h)/h\to0$ as $h\to0$ when $f$ is differentiable at $a$. No universal finite-step radius or tolerance follows.
Estimate $A$, target $v$: absolute error $|A-v|$; relative error $|A-v|/|v|$ only for $v\ne0$. Percentage error:100 times relative error.
$D_0(h)=\dfrac{f(a+h)-f(a-h)}{2h}$, $h>0$. Samples lie on both sides; full separation is $2h$.
$D_-(h)=\dfrac{f(a)-f(a-h)}{h}$, $h>0$. At a domain endpoint, label a one-sided rate.
Differentiability implies exact difference convergence. Central convergence alone does not imply differentiability: $|x|$ at zero gives $D_0(h)=0$.
For $f(x)=x^3$ at1: derivative3; $D_+(h)=3+3h+h^2$; $D_0(h)=3+h^2$. These identities are not universal error formulas.
Truncation is finite-step error in exact arithmetic. Rounding/cancellation can dominate at small steps. Equal stored inputs or outputs can destroy the useful difference.
If each sampled output error has magnitude at most $\delta$: contribution at most $2\delta/h$ forward/backward, $\delta/h$ central. Excludes truncation and other errors.
State model/domain, base input/units, formula, steps, independent reference, observed errors, edge cases and limitations. A finite table is not a universal bound.
